authorship: Hand-authored Stop, natural-end, replay, and interruption witnesses over docs/X1_TRANSPORT_CONTRACT.md sections 6-7. No production transport code exists or was consulted.

expected.law: The stop receipt resolves only after every X0 retirement receipt reported noFutureAttackPostcondition; the fake audio log contains zero attacks with start times after the stop retirement time.

cases.title: One hundred rapid play/stop cycles on one graph

expected.law: Each cycle crosses two generation boundaries; after the final stop the registry is empty, no attack follows any stop, and no voice is retired twice. This is the L-AUDIO-01 legacy regression witness.

cases.title: Stop while previewing retires both owner kinds
cases.scenario: A progression is playing and a preview is sounding when stop is admitted.

expected.law: Global Stop retires the progression generation and every preview through their X0 selectors before publishing ready.

cases.title: Preview release during playback leaves the progression untouched
cases.scenario: release-preview is admitted while the progression plays.

expected.law: Preview release is preview-scoped: no progression voice, plan binding, playhead, or published status may change.

cases.title: Natural end publishes ready at the run start beat

expected.law: Scheduling stops, tails decay naturally, and every voice is absent from the registry by eight seconds after the final note-off while the persistent graph remains ready.

cases.title: Replay during a residual tail
cases.scenario: play is admitted 0.5 s after a natural end while release/reverb tails are still audible.

expected.law: The old voice generation is retired before the new run's first attack; the new epoch begins on the same graph. This is the end-then-immediate-replay witness.

cases.title: Browser interruption freezes musical time
cases.scenario: The platform reports interrupted while playing at exact beat 5/4.

expected.law: The playhead freezes at the last computed beat; suspended wall time never advances musical time; the sounding epoch is retired so no pre-interruption callback can act.

cases.title: Interruption recovery resumes from the stored beat
cases.scenario: A trusted resume gesture arrives after X1-STOP-007.

expected.law: Recovery re-anchors a new epoch at the stored exact beat rather than replaying stale callbacks; pre-interruption callbacks are generation-dead.

cases.title: Import while playing retires before publishing
cases.scenario: replace-plan with a new binding is admitted while playing with an active preview.

expected.law: Replacement retires progression and preview voices and awaits their receipts before the replacement binding becomes visible; a stale attack from the old plan after replacement is impossible.

cases.title: New-document replacement to an empty transport
cases.scenario: replace-plan with a null binding is admitted while paused.

expected.law: A null binding empties the transport; a subsequent play without a fresh binding refuses as a mismatch instead of replaying the retired plan.
Dispose clears the control timer, retires everything through the X0 page-teardown path, publishes nothing, and every later command refuses with transport.disposed.

cases.title: Engine fault during a command settles as fault
cases.scenario: X0 faults while a play command awaits its first attack receipt.

expected.law: The command settles with fault termination, the state machine enters fault, exactly one failed notification is published with a stable code, and only a trusted reinitialization recovers.
